summary: I fixed a bug where a one-time safety-stop message was saved as a task and shown again at the start of the next session.

story.title: Stop old warnings from coming back as tasks
story.lead: ECC saves a short summary at the end of each coding session and shows it at the start of the next one. A safety-stop message was ending up in that summary.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: When a response was stopped by the safety classifier, the notice was saved as if the user had asked for it. The next session then showed it again as a past task, which could trigger the same warning repeatedly.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: I made the summary step ignore messages that start with that safety-stop notice, while keeping any normal message that only mentions the phrase in the middle of a sentence.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three tests for this; the session-end test file passes (21 of 21) and two of the new tests fail without the fix. I could not trigger a real safety stop, so the notice shape comes from the issue report.

title: Stopped the first command from timing out while a sandbox starts
summary: I fixed a bug where a command sent to a sandbox that was still starting up was treated as a one-off job and timed out, instead of running in a proper terminal.
cvLine: Fixed deferred sandbox startup in an AI security-testing agent so backends declare terminal (PTY) support up front and the first shell command keeps its interactive session; added regression tests, including one on the SDK's real local sandbox client

story.title: Make the first command work while the sandbox is still starting
story.lead: Strix can start its sandbox in the background so the agent does not have to wait. Until it finished starting, it told the tools that terminals were not available.

steps.heading: The problem
steps.text: While the sandbox was still starting, it reported that it had no terminal support. The agent library checked this straight away, so it left out the tool for typing into a running command and ran the first command as a one-off job. That command then hit a hard time limit and never returned a session to continue with.

steps.heading: My fix
steps.text: Each sandbox backend now says up front whether it supports terminals, and the built-in Docker one does. The still-starting sandbox repeats that answer until it is ready, then goes back to asking the real sandbox. Backends that do not say anything behave as before.

steps.heading: The outcome
steps.text: I added three tests, including the bug report's reproduction using the library's real local sandbox. The test file passes with 13 tests. The full suite has the same 19 failures as the main branch, and the code checks (ruff, mypy, bandit) pass.
